newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy sets ENI 3rd tranche max share price.
newsitem.headline: Italy sets ENI 3rd tranche max share price.

text.p: The Italian treasury said on Saturday it had fixed a maximum share price of 9,325 lire for the third tranche public offer of energy giant ENI.
The Italian public offer of 400 million shares will take place from Monday, June 23 to Friday, June 27.

The Treasury said it would fix the definitive share price on June 28 and it would be the lower of the maximum price or the closing price on Friday, June 27, less a three percent discount on the market price to the public.
ENI stock closed on a sharply higher Milan stock exchange on Friday at 9,468 lire, the blue-chip share accounting for over one trillion lire of total traded volume of over five trillion lire.

The Treasury, which after ENI's first two tranche sales holds 69.1 percent of ENI capital, said the third global offer of some one billion shares was the biggest operation of its kind so far this year.
A Treasury statement said that ENI stock gave an annual yield of around 16 percent.
At current share prices, the total offer was expected to raise some 10 trillion lire.

Italian investors subscribing to the offer, apart from a three percent discount on the market price of the share, would get 10 free shares for every 100 bought if they kept them for at least one year.
A further 300 million were earmarked for Italian and foreign institutional investors outside north America, with some 150 million shares reserved for U.S. and Canadian institutions.
The 12.5 percent offer could rise to 14.4 percent if the so-called "green shoe" option to cope with heavy demand was exercised, the Treasury said.
The maximum price was aimed at protecting subscribers from possible upward surges of the stock during the offer period.
The global co-ordinators, Italian bank IMI and CSFB, are expected to decide on use of the green shoe option after the U.S. roadshow ends next Friday.
But industry sources said given the expected success of the third tranche offer, the option was seen as likely.
ENI goes ex-dividend on Monday, equal to 240 lire.
